title: Reunion

location.name: Main Hall of the New Temple (Gathering and Reunion Realm)
location.kind: the harbor temple used as a community gathering hall, plus its grounds at the forest edge and a meadow
location.real_analog: a waterfront church hall turned community hall (Canton/Fells Point, Baltimore) with Canton Waterfront Park lawn for the football; a wooded park edge for the tree beats
near: the new temple (same building as poem 11)

situation: Decades later the POET hosts friends and events in the new temple; archival photos of his circle are reenacted there. The guests are his brothers and friends, laughing, hugging and shouting, then spilling outside to the trees, a meadow and finally a porch light. The EX is absent. The outdoor grounds and porch come from the spine imagery, not the treatment (inferred placement).
time_of_day: compressed across decades; the hall in warm light, then the grounds at twilight and dusk, ending at a lit porch
weather_light: soft hall light under dim rafters; green twilight through the canopy; cool dusk with visible breath; golden sunset on the meadow

set_pieces.name: Welcome home in the hall
set_pieces.what_happens: Friends arrive under a welcome-home banner; laughter and hugs with no reason; the circle forms.
lines: less time for words and more space for laughter
set_pieces.camera: wide master from the rafters, then handheld into the hugging circle
set_pieces.position: main hall floor of the temple

set_pieces.name: Loud voices, overheard hearts
set_pieces.what_happens: Voices peak; a chest-level glow pulses with every shout.
lines: loud voices so our hearts can be overheard
set_pieces.camera: tight chest-height mediums, shallow focus, fast cuts on laughter

set_pieces.name: The empty rooms of the afterlife
set_pieces.what_happens: The POET's mind drifts up into the rafters; a back room of empty chairs stands for the friends who are gone.
lines: My mind drifts into the darkness of our afterlives
set_pieces.camera: tilt up into dim rafters; static wide of the dusty backroom
set_pieces.position: rafters and a side backroom of the temple

set_pieces.name: Hourglasses and the group photo (archival reenactment)
set_pieces.what_happens: Everyone freezes for a group photo, each holding an hourglass of burning sand; old photos reenacted, maps of shared routes.
lines: each holding our glasses of burning sands
set_pieces.camera: locked frontal group tableau matched to the archival photo; macro on falling grains
set_pieces.position: the hall's front, posed like the source photographs

set_pieces.name: Trees at the forest edge
set_pieces.what_happens: Outside, friends touch tree trunks under picnic lights; breath mingles in cool dusk; memories project onto fog.
lines: grateful to every living tree in the forest
set_pieces.camera: low angle up into the canopy; slow lateral track along the trunks
set_pieces.position: temple grounds where the hills' woods begin (inferred)

set_pieces.name: Brotherhood chain
set_pieces.what_happens: Wrists interlock, heads lean together; one ear pressed to the next brother's chest.
lines: we can place our ears upon the next brother's soul
set_pieces.camera: profile tracking shot down the listening chain; extreme close-up of an ear on a chest
set_pieces.position: a sandy path from the grounds toward the shore

set_pieces.name: Football in the meadow, then home
set_pieces.what_happens: A football spirals across a sunset meadow; polaroids scatter; the group walks up as a porch light switches on.
lines: follow paths of hilltops and canyons
that bring us home every time
set_pieces.camera: wide golden-hour meadow with the ball arcing through frame; closing shot from behind the group toward a lit porch
set_pieces.position: meadow by the temple, ending at a front porch

arrival.from_previous: No travel: 'Decades later' the temple he rebuilt in poem 11 is full of friends and events.

departure.to_next: Daytime/sunlight: the POET wanders out of the new temple and around the harbor to a cafe.

encoding: The temple built on the ruin becomes a home that holds people: the poem answers the empty choir stands and pews of poem 3 with a full hall. This is the film's real homecoming ('brings us home every time'), staged as communion among men rather than romance, which is why it must happen inside the rebuilt sacred place. The outdoor beats are inferred from the spine.
evidence: treatment: "POET hosts friends and events with friends in new temple as described."
treatment: "[source material: archival photos reenacted in new temple.]"
poem 12: "grateful to every living tree in the forest for the shared years"

open_questions: The spine scatters the reunion across a gym, a ballroom, a forest, a meadow and a porch; the treatment keeps it in the new temple. This bible treats the outdoor beats as temple grounds (inferred).
Who the friends are (family? the MOTHER and FATHER of poem 9?) is unspecified beyond 'brother'.
Is 'decades later' a flash-forward from poem 11 or a montage of many reunions? The time of day is therefore loose.
The map draws the GATHERING AND REUNION REALM on the Baltimere (west) side but puts the REUNION node in CENTER.
